agree.reason: A GM who believes the renovation drove the scores gets only the claim that the desk 'helped'. The memo leaves out the 7.9-to-8.2 rise before the renovation started, the zero uncovered shifts and the overtime under plan, so it gives him little reason to choose her over the larger-hotel candidate.

honest.reason: It correctly drops the 'main reason' claim and admits she has never managed a budget, but it predicts without evidence that the team will keep the score up 'after the renovation stops being new', and it presents the payroll savings as fact when they are inferred.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the 64% and 36% turnover rates and the four fewer departures, but it never states the 44% cut in training shifts and never splits the score rise into its before-renovation and after-renovation parts, which is the split that matters most.

right_comparison.reason: The outside hire is described only by what they lack (this team, this hotel), and their larger-hotel experience is left out. The renovation comparison misses the fact that the score was already rising before the work began.

qualification.reason: The budget hedge ('work through the next payroll budget with you') gives no date, no measurable check and no consequence if it fails, and it leaves out the available commitments: the finance course within 3 months and weekly sessions with the controller.

objections.reason: The budget gap is met head-on, but the renovation objection gets only a soft assertion when a decisive fact was available, and the outside candidate's real advantage is never acknowledged or answered.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo as asked, but it uses role titles instead of the names Daniela Ruiz and Mark Ellison, and it repeats the 'From:' line at the end.
